slice: Sixth fill of uncovered pre-2020 off-road years: Husqvarna FX 350 2017, 2016 TE/FE range, TX 125 2018, KTM 250 XC-F 2018 (knowledge push 2026-11)

records.topic: FX 350 2017: how it differs from the FC 350
records.statement: The 2017 FX 350 is the cross-country version of the FC 350: a six-speed gearbox (one more than the FC), the WP AER 48 air fork with air on the left leg and damping on the right, a clear 2.2-gallon tank with the extra fuel carried low, an 18-inch rear wheel, handguards, a Magura clutch and a lithium-ion battery for the starter. The air fork is 3.6 lb lighter than the 4CS it replaced.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2017 Husqvarna FX 350 first ride

records.statement: On the 2017 FX 350 the air fork is plush off-road and a little soft for motocross. To stop it bottoming, raise the air pressure, stiffen the clicker, or both. Check the pressure with the supplied gauge before every ride.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2017 Husqvarna FX 350 first ride

records.statement: Of the 2017 pair, the FX 350 feels light and free-revving, like a 250 with far more power, and keeps pulling to very high rpm. It lacks the 450's low-end, does not chug well at very low revs and stalls in tight technical sections unless the clutch is covered; extra flywheel weight was suggested for hard enduro. The FX 450 feels heavier and more stable, has more low-end torque, lugs to a crawl without stalling and finds traction better on technical ground, helped by its two maps and traction control. Neither has a spark arrestor.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - 2017 Husqvarna FX350 and FX450 first impression

records.topic: FX 350 and FX 450 2017 stock suspension limits
records.statement: Both the 2017 FX 350 and FX 450 are soft on jump faces, harsh on landings and bottom on large jumps as delivered; hard motocross use needs suspension work. The 450 is slightly firm on slow, technical off-road sections.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - 2017 Husqvarna FX350 and FX450 first impression

records.statement: For 2016 all TE and FE models got a 22 mm front axle in place of the 26 mm one, triple-clamp offset increased 2 mm to 22 mm, a revised 4CS fork setting and a new shock setting, open fork protectors, new front and rear brake discs, lighter spokes, a grippier seat cover, a map switch as standard and four bar-mount positions. The FE 350 also got a modified lubrication system (better oiling in extreme conditions and protection against overfilling), a new gearbox input-shaft bearing for smoother shifts and a new shift-lever bolt. The FE 450 and FE 501 got an updated DDS clutch with a basket 80 g lighter. No model-specific changes were listed for the TE 250 or TE 300.

source.name: Cycle News - 2016 Husqvarna off-road and dual sport first look

records.statement: The 2018 TX 125 is a 124.8 cc (54 x 54.5 mm) kick-start two-stroke with a six-speed gearbox, 300 mm of front and 330 mm of rear travel, a 10-litre tank, a 960 mm seat, a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheel, and a dry weight of 92 kg.

The 2018 250 XC-F is a 249.9 cc DOHC four-valve engine (78 x 52.3 mm, 14.4:1) with Keihin fuel injection and a six-speed gearbox. It uses the WP AER air fork (310 mm travel) and a linkage shock (300 mm), holds 2.3 gallons, has a 960 mm seat and a listed dry weight of 218.7 lb.
